source.name: Ice: The Secret Ingredient That Makes or Breaks Your Cocktails

slides.kicker: Most home bars get this wrong.
slides.title: Ice is an ingredient
slides.subtitle: Not a garnish. Not an afterthought.

slides.title: What ice actually does
slides.note: Five jobs — and only one of them is "cold".

slides.title: Three kinds of ice
slides.note: Surface area is the whole story: more surface, faster dilution.

slides.title: Water is not the enemy
paragraphs: Ice doesn't only chill a drink — it melts into it. That water is doing real work: it binds the ingredients together, softens the edge of the alcohol, and opens up aromas that stay locked shut when a drink is too strong or too cold.
A cocktail served with no dilution isn't purer. It's unfinished.

slides.title: Match the ice to the drink
slides.note: Spirit-forward and slow-sipped? Go big. Long and refreshing? Go small.
